_note: The LIVE LOGS wire core - the pure half of dev.stream (proposals/live-logs.md) that must not drift between renderers because it decides what leaves the device and how both ends of the relay agree. Row folds APPLY the telemetry scrubber at enqueue (the rules themselves stay pinned by Conformance/telemetry/scrub.json - cases here prove the application, never re-pin the rules). The queue is drop-oldest with a counted drop; the ack fold is how a device knows to keep sending (viewers watching), pause the wire (nobody watching - the ring keeps recording), or stop (the pairing expired); the ring is the relay's durable cursor law (monotonic seq, bounded replay, gap told to the reader - the realtime.ts contract over live rows). Twins: TS packages/kernel/src/livelogs.ts - Kotlin :core LiveLogs.kt - Swift Engine/iOS/LiveLogs.swift.

rows.name: a log entry folds to a log row
a console warn keeps its level
the scrubber applies at the fold - a bearer token never reaches the wire
an email in a log line is redacted at the fold
a message longer than the cap is clipped to messageCap
the cap counts UTF-16 code units and never strands a high surrogate
an ambient error folds to an error row
a call failure with no message omits the key rather than sending null
an uncaught throw keeps its origin - the viewer's CRASH tag rides it
a kernel line folds whole - stamp and all
a kernel line is scrubbed too

batch.name: the batch body - version, session, monotonic index, rows

ack.name: viewers watching - keep sending, deadline follows ttl
nobody watching for idleAckPause acks - the wire pauses, the session survives
a viewer returning resets the idle count and resumes the wire
a refused ack changes nothing - transport failure belongs to the queue backoff
the deadline passing expires the session

queue.name: a batch peeks - only the ack removes
a peeked batch is pinned - the cap drops behind it, never inside it
queue._note: The exact-retry law: a batch in flight is identity - the relay's replay refusal and the driver's ack both assume attempt 2 carries the SAME rows as attempt 1. So while a batch is peeked, drop-oldest skips the pinned head: the cap evicts the oldest UNPINNED row, and when every present row is in flight the NEWCOMER is the drop. Without this, pushing at cap during an outage shifted rows out of the in-flight batch, the retry carried different rows under the same n, and the ack then removed rows that were never sent.

queue.name: a fully-pinned queue drops the newcomer, counted

ring.name: seq is assigned monotonically from 1 and reads resume after a cursor
a replayed batch index is refused once - retries cannot duplicate rows
the bound evicts oldest and a lagging reader is told about the gap
limit caps a read and the next cursor continues it
